nodes.name: Lemma 6.15
nodes.statement: For every ideal $\mathcal{I}$ and $A \in \mathrm{ulm}\left(\mathcal{I}\right)$, $R^{\langle A,\mathcal{I} \rangle}_{\mathcal{I}}: \LF{\langle A,\mathcal{I} \rangle}{X} \to \LF{\mathcal{I}}{X}$ is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.12
nodes.statement: For all ideals $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathcal{C}\ell\left(X\right)$ and subsets $Y \subseteq X$, $R_{\mathcal{I}} \oplus Q_{\mathcal{I}}: \LF{Y} \oplus_1 \ell^1_{\mathcal{I}}\left( Y \right) \to \LF{\mathcal{I},Y}$ is a quotient map; it maps the open ball onto the open ball.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.21
nodes.statement:
Assume $X$ is discrete. Fix an ideal $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathcal{C}\ell\left(X\right)$ such that $\mathcal{F}in \subseteq \mathcal{I}$ and $R^{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{F}in}$ is injective. Set $\mathcal{J} := \mathrm{ulm}\left(\mathcal{I}\right)$ so that Theorem 6.13 implies $R^{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{F}in}$ is also injective (for example, $\mathcal{I} = \mathcal{F}in_n$ and $\mathcal{J} = \mathcal{F}in_{n+1}$). For any $p \in X$, $r \in (0,\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{J}}\left(p\right))$, $u \in \LF{\mathcal{I}}{X}$ such that $\supp{u} \cap B_{r}(p)$ is finite, and sequence $v_n \in \LF{\mathcal{J}}{X}$ such that $\sup_n \|v_n\|_{\mathcal{J}} < 1$ and $R^{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{I}}(v_n) \to u$, and $c \in (0,1)$, there exists another sequence $\tilde{v}_n$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item $\sup_n \|\tilde{v}_n\|_{\mathcal{J}} < 1$,
\item $R^{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{I}}(\tilde{v}_n) \to u$,
\item $\supp{\tilde{v}_n} \subseteq \supp{v_n}$,
\item and $\supp{\tilde{v}_n} \cap B_{cr}(p) = \supp{u} \cap B_{cr}(p)$.
\end{itemize}

nodes.name: Lemma 6.16
nodes.statement:
For any ideal $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathcal{C}\ell\left(X\right)$, $Y \subseteq X$, $c \in (0,1)$, and $u \in \LF{\mathcal{I}}{Y}$ with $\|u\|_{\mathcal{I}} < 1$ there exist, setting $\rho(p,q) := c \min\{\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{I}}\left(p\right),\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{I}}\left(q\right)\}$, $\{b_{(p,q)}\}_{(p,q) \in Y^2: d(p,q) \leq \rho(p,q)}$, and $\{\tilde{a}_p\}_{p \in Y} \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$u = \sum_{\substack{(p,q) \in Y^2 \\ d(p,q) \leq \rho(p,q)}}b_{(p,q)}(\delta_p-\delta_q) + \sum_{p \in Y} \tilde{a}_{p} \delta_p$$
and
$$\sum_{\substack{(p,q) \in Y^2 \\ d(p,q) \leq \rho(p,q)}}|b_{(p,q)}|d(p,q) + \sum_{p \in Y} |\tilde{a}_{p}|\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{I}}\left(p\right) < 3c^{-1}.$$

nodes.name: Lemma 6.17
nodes.statement: For every ideal $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathcal{C}\ell\left(X\right)$ and $u \in \LF{\mathcal{I}}{X}$ with $\|u\| < 1$, there exist $\tilde{w} \in \LF{X}$ and $\tilde{a} \in \ell^1_{\mathcal{I}}\left( X \right)$ such that $u = R_{\mathcal{I}}(\tilde{w}) + Q_{\mathcal{I}}(\tilde{a})$, $\|\tilde{w}\| + \|\tilde{a}\|_{\ell^1_{\mathcal{I}}\left( X \right)} < 1$, and the following separation property is satisfied: whenever $\tilde{a}_p \cdot \tilde{a}_q < 0$ for some $p \neq q \in X$, then $d(p,q) \geq (\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{I}}\left(p\right)+\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{I}}\left(q\right))/2$.

nodes.name: Lemma 6.22
Lemma 6.18
nodes.statement: Assume $X$ is countable with enumeration $X = \{p_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$. Fix an ideal $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathcal{C}\ell\left(X\right)$ and set $\mathcal{J} := \mathrm{ulm}\left(\mathcal{I}\right)$. For every $u \in \LF{\mathcal{I}}{X}$ with $\|u\| < 1$ and collection of radii $\{r_p\}_{p \in X}$ with $r_p \in (0,\mathrm{rad}_{\mathcal{J}}\left(p\right))$, there exist $w \in \LF{X}$ and $a \in \ell^1_{\mathcal{I}}\left( X \right)$ such that $u = R_{\mathcal{I}}(w) + Q_{\mathcal{I}}(a)$, $\|w\| + \|a\|_{\ell^1_{\mathcal{I}}\left( X \right)} < 1$, and $\supp{a} \cap B_{r_p}(p)$ is finite for each $p \in X$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.23
nodes.statement: Assume $X$ is countable with enumeration $X = \{p_i\}_{i=1}^\infty$. Assume $X$ is discrete. Fix an ideal $\mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathcal{C}\ell\left(X\right)$ such that $\mathcal{F}in \subseteq \mathcal{I}$ and $R^{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{F}in}$ is injective. Set $\mathcal{J} := \mathrm{ulm}\left(\mathcal{I}\right)$ so that Theorem 6.13 implies $R^{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{F}in}$ is also injective (for example, $\mathcal{I} = \mathcal{F}in_n$ and $\mathcal{J} = \mathcal{F}in_{n+1}$). The map $R^{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{I}}: \LF{\mathcal{J},X} \to \LF{\mathcal{I}}{X}$ is a 7-semi-embedding.
